theorem_title: Refined parent and child have equivalent convergence
natural_language_statement:
Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$. Write $\mathcal C(n)$ for the assertion that $T^j(n)=1$ for some $j\in\mathbb N$. For natural parameters $L,\varepsilon,z$, put $A=4z+2\varepsilon+1$, $P=2^LA-1$, and $Q=3\cdot2^{L-2}A-1$. When $L<2$, the exponent $L-2$ uses truncated natural subtraction.

Assume $L\ge2$, $\varepsilon\le1$, and $\varepsilon\equiv L\pmod2$. Then

$$
\mathcal C(P)\iff\mathcal C(Q).
$$

The result transfers convergence across the guarded shared orbit point without asserting convergence on either side.

formal_statement:
theorem CollatzWork.refinedParent_converges_iff_child (L epsilon z : Nat) (hL : 2 ≤ L)
    (hepsilon : epsilon ≤ 1)
    (hparity : epsilon % 2 = L % 2) :
    Converges (refinedParent L epsilon z) ↔
      Converges (refinedChild L epsilon z) := by sorry
